description: A two-panel composite figure; both panels share a horizontal Strain [%] axis (0-0.3, gridlines every 0.05) but plot different quantities for the same pre-strained specimens, identified by the letter call-outs A-E. (a) Stress [MPa] (0-400, 50 MPa gridlines) versus Strain [%]: five solid curves (magenta/pink, green, dark navy, grey, and a second green) are superimposed below about 0.05% strain and then fan out; at 0.3% strain the upper curves reach roughly 375 MPa while the lowest green curve plateaus near 225 MPa. Large letters A, B, C, D, E with crossing leader lines point at individual curves. (b) Elastic modulus [GPa] (0-250, 50 GPa gridlines) versus Strain [%]: the apparent modulus of each specimen falls steeply with strain, a noisy curve labelled E staying near 200 GPa before dropping, curves B and C descending from ~200 GPa to below 50 GPa, and a red dashed straight line decreasing almost linearly from roughly 190 GPa to roughly 20 GPa. Taken together, the panels show that the gradient (apparent Young's modulus) of each stress-strain curve decreases continuously with increasing strain in the elastic/near-elastic region, and that the rate of this decrease differs between specimens. No numeric data labels are printed; all values must be read from gridlines.

observations.observation: Figure 4 is a two-panel composite: (a) is a stress-strain plot with axes Stress [MPa] (0-400) versus Strain [%] (0-0.3), and (b) is an elastic-modulus-versus-strain plot with axes Elastic modulus [GPa] (0-250) versus Strain [%] (0-0.3).
Panel (a) contains five solid stress-strain curves (magenta/pink, green, dark navy, grey, and a second green); they are nearly coincident below about 0.05% strain and separate above it.
In panel (a) the upper curves reach approximately 375 MPa at 0.3% strain, whereas the lowest green curve plateaus at about 225 MPa.

Large call-out letters A, B, C, D and E with leader lines annotate individual curves in panel (a); the letters sit near the middle of the plot and several leader lines cross, so the letter-to-curve assignment is partly ambiguous.
Panel (b) contains a red dashed straight line that decreases monotonically from roughly 190 GPa near 0% strain to roughly 20 GPa at about 0.27% strain.

In panel (b) one noisy curve (associated with letter E) stays near 200 GPa up to about 0.2% strain before falling, while other curves annotated B and C drop from about 200 GPa to below 50 GPa over the same strain range.
The caption labels (a) as 'the stress-strain curves measured by strain gauge' and (b) as 'the variation in the gradient of the curves'.
The caption names the figure 'Variation in Young's modulus in the elastic region for pre-strained specimens'.

The citing text states that the stress-strain curve was measured with a load cell and a strain gauge up to a strain of 1%, and that the elastic modulus was obtained from the stress-strain curves within the elastic deformation region.
The strain axis of both panels stops at 0.3%, which is shorter than the 1% strain mentioned in the citing sentence; the panels therefore show only the low-strain portion.
No numeric data values are printed anywhere in either panel; all readings must be taken from the axis gridlines.
Both panels show the same five-letter specimen labelling set (A-E), indicating that the modulus curves in (b) correspond to the stress-strain curves in (a).

subfigures.description: Stress [MPa] (0-400, 50 MPa gridlines) versus Strain [%] (0-0.3, 0.05 gridlines) plot of five solid curves in magenta/pink, green, dark navy, grey and a second green. Curves coincide below ~0.05% strain then diverge; the highest reach ~375 MPa at 0.3% strain, the lowest ~225 MPa. Call-out letters A, B, C, D, E with leader lines point to the individual curves.

Elastic modulus [GPa] (0-250, 50 GPa gridlines) versus Strain [%] (0-0.3) plot showing the strain-dependence of the gradient. Several solid/dashed curves (a noisy high one near 200 GPa, and others falling to <50 GPa) plus a red dashed straight line descending from ~190 GPa to ~20 GPa. Letters A-E with leader lines annotate the curves; the exact curve each of B and C denotes is partly ambiguous.
